$comment: The queue is a partial order, not a list. Permissions depends on nothing and blocks four; Documentation Files blocks Projects List; Enterprise is parallel. The expected order is verified against the deps in this file, so the fixture cannot silently drift from its own graph.
tieBreak: no unshipped deps first; ties by project id ascending — declared, because 'whatever order the store returned' is how a queue becomes non-deterministic

expected.why: The refusal names the blocking id, not 'not ready' — otherwise the operator goes looking at the wrong workstream.
One hop is enough to refuse; the chain is what the queue renders, not what the error recites.

expected.message: perms-1862 is already live on macbook (generation 3)
expected.why: Same rule as adoption: two owners is the bug, and the message names the holder and the generation.

expected.message: dependency cycle: a -> b -> c -> a
expected.why: Humans eventually create one. A cycle reported as 'blocked' hides it forever; the refusal must name the loop so somebody can break it.

assertions: expectedOrder contains every unshipped workstream exactly once and no shipped one
no entry appears before a dependency it needs
blockedBy lists every unshipped dependency, not just the first
a shipped dependency is satisfied and does not appear in blockedBy
the cycle case is refused rather than resolved by ignoring an edge
